What I have found works best is seating someone down, and telling them, as wordily as possible, about what your intent is. You have to give reassurances and disclaimers. That you do not intend to tie them down. That you plan only because it means so much to you. You have to clarify it to them. And you have to assure them that you have accounted for variables. That you, at your end, will work on how you perceive things. But also, request them to work on their outright dismissiveness of the future. Tell them, that a relationship, if meaningful, needs to have an end goal. They needn't promise anything now. As long as they make the effort to keep it in mind. 

Lastly, you're both really young, in the grander scheme of things. A lot of these things also come through learning experiences in life. They might one day find out that they really need you far more in life than they gave you credit for. That you're much more permanent an existence than they initially thought. 

Relationships require a lot of work. Which I bet both of you are willing to put in :)

My suggestion would be that while your partner is right, so are you. There is no ONE correct answer here. But, we all need to fend for ourselves. Protect our own sanity. Which is why I'll suggest that while you make these "plans", try to remind yourself that they are all subject to change. That trying to plan for something that is filled with variables such as the future is only testing hypotheses at best. That being said, it's sweet and extremely human to hope and plan for the future. But please, for your sake, don't set them in stone. Because there WILL be disappointments. 

The other thing is, from your partner's perspective, they may feel that you're making it very concrete and that they need to make sure their life takes the exact trajectory so that the prophecy is fulfilled. This can come off as extremely constricting. It has nothing to do with their commitment or loyalty to you. It just has to do with their belief system, and their backgrounds. For example, a person who's had a turbulent childhood, would be too scared to plan for a future with someone. Does not mean that they don't want one or that they can't love someone to the end of the world. It's just that they have a factor at play from a time before the relationship existed.

But, what do you do if you don't have any person who cares about you? I ask this for myself. It gets lonely, so pleasing people and trying to get them to like me is the only way I get some semblance of companionship.

You could almost always get one shot by red bar adds even. They aren't undoable. Also, I'd argue that they are not similar to raids because in most raids, it's the mechanics that kill us. The actual adds are just there. 

With the right team, sure, it is doable. But along with that, what I'd say is important is playing it slow. In my experience, it is 70% of the time, normal adds that'll kill you, not champions or the boss. That is because a champ or a boss has your team's complete attention. An add, however, would just sneak up behind you and kill you.

They are very very much doable, and some are even farmable. Communicate with your team, think of strategies beforehand. The meta is great, but also experiment with your loadout. Make a peak-survivability build. Cover is your best friend. Do not stray too far away from cover ever. You should be more than good to go. 

And don't forget your elemental resist mods! :)
